title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Default autotune profiles for batching/caching and quantization added; new unit-economics endpoints and dashboard components. No user-facing API breaking changes. Backwards compatible defaults, opt-out via feature flag.
description:
Summary: Adds default autotune profiles and heuristics for batching and KV caching, introduces per-model quantization profile presets, and ships initial unit-economics (UEcon) tooling support in the console and backend. Motivation: Customers running mixed workloads were repeatedly hitting suboptimal defaults (small batches + aggressive cache TTLs) which increased per‑token cost. This PR centralizes sensible defaults, exposes opt-outs, and surfaces UEcon telemetry so we can iterate on unit cost targets.

Changes (high-level):
- runtime/batcher: introduce adaptive_min_batch_size and sliding-window latency target for continuous batching.
- runtime/cache: introduce default KV cache TTL and prefix-aware prewarm heuristics; add metrics for cache hit/miss cost impact.
- autotune/service: new autotune profiles that generate recommended batching/caching configs based on observed qps/latency/cost.
- quant/profiles: ship three presets (fp16, int8_trusted, int8_aggressive) and mapping rules by model size and instruction-following load.
- console/uecon: add backend endpoints (/api/v1/uecon/recommendations) and a dashboard card that surfaces per-route unit cost, suggested savings, and one-click apply for recommendations (behind flag).
- telemetry: add derived metrics (tokens_per_second, cost_per_token_est) and a UEcon aggregation job used by recommendations.
- tests: unit and integration tests for autotune generator and batcher e2e smoke tests.

Behavioral details and rationale: 
- Batching: default_min_batch_size increased from 1 to 4 and a latency-target-based sliding window reduces overly small batches for high qps routes. This reduces per-token overhead for many NLP workloads while preserving tail latency SLOs.
- KV cache: TTL defaults moved from 5s to 30s for prefixable requests; prewarm heuristic warms hot prefixes when observed qps > threshold. We added a weight-based eviction tweak to keep memory footprint steady.
- Autotune: generator now consumes 1h of telemetry and outputs candidate profiles ranked by expected cost delta and latency regression risk. Recommendations include an estimated monthly savings and confidence band.
- Quantization: three presets cover common tradeoffs; int8_aggressive has higher quality regression risk but greater cost reduction. Mapping rules prefer fp16 for small (<3B) models with latency‑sensitive routes.

Feature flags and opt-out: all automated recommendation application is behind the feature flag uecon.auto_apply (disabled by default). The console shows recommendations by default but requires explicit apply to change serving configs.

Testing and CI: 
- Local unit tests: 232 passed
- Integration: initial e2e smoke that exercises batcher + cache + autotune generator; flaky on first run (timing) so we added a retry + timeout adjustment.
- CI pipeline: build -> lint -> unit -> integration (uecon) -> canary smoke. First run: integration job failed (timeout) on 2026-02-12; retried after adding a 10s buffer to test harness and passed on 2026-02-13.

Review thread (highlights):
- Ethan Zhang (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Can we ensure the default_min_batch_size change is gated per-model? I'm worried about small, low-latency models that would regress. Please add a per-model override and doc note."
- Priya (author): "Good point — added per-model override in services/autotune/config.rs and documented in runtime/batcher/README.md (see commit 5f12a9). Autotune will not overwrite explicit per-model overrides unless the user enables uecon.auto_apply."
- Lina Rodriguez: "Quant presets look good. Request: add a short presubmit that runs a quality regression check on the sample eval set for int8_aggressive."
- Priya: "Added lightweight quality check (samples/quant_regressions.yaml) and a CI gate that fails only if drop >2% for production-tier models. Disabled for draft models."
- Marco Silva: "Telemetry derivation looks correct; suggest exposing cache hit/miss cost multiplier as a label on request traces to make review easier."
- Priya: "Added trace label and example instrumentation in runtime/cache. Also added a console trace view example to the UEcon card docs."
- Final approvals: Ethan (approved), Lina (approved after fix), Marco (approved).

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Customers with explicit per-route or per-model configs are unaffected unless they opt into applying recommendations.
- Default behavior changes (batching TTLs) apply only to routes with no explicit config.
- Admins can disable recommendations or auto‑apply via feature flags in the console or config file.

Metrics observed in staging (A/B test for 48h across ~200 routes):
- median cost_per_token_est: −11.8% (control vs recommended)
- p95 latency: +0.9% (within SLO)
- cache_hit_rate: +6.1% for prefixable routes
- estimated monthly savings (projected): $9.3k across the test tenant

Security and compliance: no secret handling changes. UEcon endpoints require admin scope and are behind RBAC check. Added audit entries on apply actions.

Deployment plan: staged rollout; console UI behind feature flag; backend recommendation generator started as a canary service in us-west-2 then rolled globally after 48h and sanity checks.

Merge: squash and merge after approvals and CI green. Changelog entry added to releases/notes/2026-02.md.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-790: add model-specific latency budgets to the autotune inputs to better balance p95 vs cost.
- PM-313: expand UEcon dashboard to show historical trendlines and cohort comparisons.
- ENG-791: offline job to run deeper quality regression tests for aggressive quant presets.
